statusNote: Early preview. The web components are the mature surface; the iOS adapter and these decisions are still being iterated, so expect layout rules and chrome to change between releases. Report what looks wrong rather than patching around it.

designPolicy.principle: Sable first. Every screen is built from Sable components in the chosen preset. The adapter supplies only the iOS system chrome Sable has no equivalent for: the app frame and status bar, the navigation bar, the tab bar and sheet presentation.
chrome: navigation bar: title, large title, back, bar actions
sable: every control: Switch, Input, Slider, SearchInput, Select, Checkbox, Button
lists and rows: Card, CardList, Entity
designPolicy.rule: Never import from konsta. Chrome comes from @sableui/react/ios; anything else is a Sable component. If Sable lacks something a screen needs, report it as a library gap rather than reaching for a native control.
designPolicy.styling: One document: Tailwind, Sable styles.css, the preset, then @sableui/react/ios/styles.css. The chrome reads the preset; Sable content follows it as on the web. Align content to px-(--ios-inset).
layout: A sheet owns what a card owns on a page: the surface, the edge padding and the actions. IosSheet provides a "sheet" PresentationProvider, and Sable lays its content out for it; do not restyle it by hand.

Actions: mark a footer that holds only buttons with <CardFooter actions>. In a sheet it becomes a full-width stack pinned to the bottom, the primary on top, every button at the cta height. A footer with a caption, a price or a list affordance stays unmarked.

Surface: pass framed={false} to a block in a sheet; a flat card there bleeds its padding so its content lines up with the sheet. Use background="opaque" for a form at the medium detent; keep glass for short, read-only content.

implementation.ownership: The adapter's optional peer, installed in the consuming project only for an iOS prototype. Apps never import it.

AppHeader.guidance: The screen title, back and bar actions are the iOS navigation bar. It takes the preset font and accent; keep its geometry.
